member.summary: Provides a lightweight reader-writer lock optimized for rare write operations.

remarks.para: Multiple readers can hold the lock concurrently, but writers have exclusive access. This implementation uses spin-waiting and is best suited for short critical sections.

remarks.para: Worker threads are kept alive for the lifetime of the pool to avoid wake-up overhead. Tasks are distributed via per-thread queues with work stealing for load balancing.

member.name: P:Jitter2.Parallelization.ThreadPool.CurrentWorkerIndex
member.summary: Gets the index of the worker executing on the calling thread, in [0, ).
member.remarks:
Callbacks invoked during a multithreaded step can use this to index per-worker scratch storage without synchronization, since no two workers share an index for the duration of a step. The thread that calls participates as worker 0.

member.name: P:Jitter2.World.PersistentContactManifold
member.summary: When enabled (the default), contact points and their accumulated impulses are cached between frames. This allows the solver to warm-start from the previous solution and enables the manifold to grow over several steps, which improves stability for resting contacts. When disabled, all contact data is discarded at the end of each frame and every contact is treated as brand-new. Disabling this removes all frame-to-frame contact memory at the cost of solver convergence speed.

member.name: P:Jitter2.World.SpeculativeRelaxationFactor
member.summary: A speculative contact slows a body down such that it does not penetrate or tunnel through an obstacle within one frame. The scales the slowdown, ranging from 0 (where the body stops immediately during this frame) to 1 (where the body and the obstacle just touch after the next velocity integration). A value below 1 is preferred, as the leftover velocity might be enough to trigger another speculative contact in the next frame. Default value: 0.9.

member.name: P:Jitter2.World.SpeculativeVelocityThreshold

member.name: P:Jitter2.World.RestitutionThreshold
member.summary: Approach speed a contact must exceed before restitution is applied at all. Default value: 1.0.
member.remarks:
XENGINE: this was a literal inside . It exists because a resting contact still reports a small approach velocity each step, and applying restitution to it makes a bouncy body jitter instead of settling. Exposing it is the counterpart of Unity's Physics.bounceThreshold, whose default is 2 — raising it suppresses small bounces, lowering it lets light taps bounce at the cost of settling.
